subject: Deferred-invoice private offer & channel escrow — DataMill (AWS Marketplace)
messages:
From: Evelyn Torres <evelyn.torres@datamill.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@datamill.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on AWS private offer billing cadence and reseller holdback

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with latency and the routing features. We're close to internal approval but procurement has flagged two items for the private offer on AWS Marketplace:

1) Billing cadence: DataMill runs a monthly billing close but would like to request invoicing on a 30-day deferred schedule (invoice issued at month end, payment due +30 days after month close). Will that work with a private offer flow via the marketplace?

2) Channel holdback / escrow: our reseller (ByteChannel) requires a 6% holdback on spend for 90 days as part of their onboarding. We need confirmation on whether Redwood can:
   - support a holdback amount captured as an escrow line item on the invoice; and
   - provide a reconciliation runbook so ByteChannel can reclaim the holdback if usage thresholds are met.

Can you confirm feasibility and any impacts on list price / channel margin? Also attaching our standard procurement template (see attachment).

Thanks,
Evelyn Torres
VP Finance, DataMill Inc.
Attachment: datamill-procurement-template.pdf (pdf)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Torres <evelyn.torres@datamill.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on AWS private offer billing cadence and reseller holdback

Evelyn — thanks for the clear ask and the template. Short answer: yes, we can support both items but there are operational details to align on. High-level notes below; I'll loop in Ops/Channel for the runbook.

Billing cadence (deferred invoicing):
- We can set the private offer to invoice at month-end with a Net30 payment term. For marketplace billing we map the marketplace invoice to your account and Redwood issues a settlement line in our invoice feed.
- Two caveats: (a) for metered SKUs there is a finalization lag (usage reports from AWS can take 48–72h after month close) — this means the invoice may be provisional and adjusted on a next-period true-up, and (b) list-price shown on the marketplace UI will be the committed list; the Net pricing is via private offer metadata.

Channel holdback / escrow:
- We can include an "Escrow: Channel holdback" line on Redwood's invoice representing the 6% holdback. Redwood will hold that amount in our finance ledger (not a third-party escrow provider) for a 90-day window and release upon reconciliation evidence from ByteChannel.
- Operationally we suggest: 1) ByteChannel submits claim via the reconciliation runbook (evidence = signed usage report + invoice matching), 2) Redwood Ops validates (2–3 business days), 3) funds released to ByteChannel and corresponding adjustment recorded on next invoice.

Impacts on channel margin / pricing:
- To preserve the channel margin for ByteChannel we recommend adding a 6% 'holdback line' on the invoice but keep list price and private-offer discount unchanged. Practically this reduces cash paid to the reseller at settlement until release.
- If DataMill prefers Redwood to front the 6% (i.e., Redwood pays the reseller immediately and then reclaims if thresholds not met), that's a different program and needs credit approval — typically reserved for strategic deals.

Attachments: I'm attaching a short summary of the private-offer billing flow and an escrow runbook draft for your review.

Next steps: if this model works, we propose a short operations call (30m) with ByteChannel + Redwood Ops to walk the runbook and agree SLAs for validation and release.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Cloud GTM — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-privoffer-summary.pdf (pdf), escrow-runbook-v1.md (markdown)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, Evelyn Torres <evelyn.torres@datamill.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deferred-invoice private offer & channel escrow — DataMill (AWS Marketplace)

Evelyn / team — quick ops + pricing clarifications from my side (Ben, channel ops):

Operational checklist (for the 30m runbook call):
- Which ByteChannel contact will submit reconciliation claims? Need name + email + sample signed usage report format.
- Do you require escrow to be visible in AWS billing console or only on Redwood's invoice? We support both but AWS console visibility requires a marketplace mapping and may add 2–3 business days to settlement.
- Does ByteChannel expect holdback release on a per-invoice basis or aggregated quarterly? Our recommendation is per-invoice release at 90 days to keep bookkeeping simple.

Pricing/Accounting impacts:
- The 6% holdback will be recorded as a contra-revenue line on Redwood's ledger until release. That does not change the private-offer net price to DataMill.
- If DataMill needs the reseller margin to be guaranteed (i.e., Redwood pays ByteChannel up front), we need a signed credit addendum and finance sign-off; that will likely change commercial terms (we typically reserve that for commitments > $1M ARR).

Irene — tagging you on the mapping requirements for AWS usage finalization and how adjustments appear on next-period true-ups.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Channel Operations
From: Evelyn Torres <evelyn.torres@datamill.com>

Thanks Ben / Hannah — this looks reasonable and aligns with our internal constraints. Two clarifications before we lock:

1) ByteChannel contact: Maya Singh <maya@bytechannel.io> — she will submit claims (signed usage + invoice).
2) Release cadence: ByteChannel prefers per-invoice release at 90 days. That is acceptable.

One ask on evidence: can Redwood accept a CSV export from our billing system + a signed statement from ByteChannel (simple two-line template) as acceptable reconciliation evidence? That will help speed their process.

If you confirm, we'll schedule the runbook call for Thursday 21 May (30m) and route a DocuSign addendum if needed.

Regards,
Evelyn
VP Finance, DataMill Inc.
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deferred-invoice private offer & channel escrow — DataMill (AWS Marketplace)

Evelyn / Maya — confirmed. Summary of agreed model and next steps: 

Agreed model (summary):
- Private offer via AWS Marketplace; invoice generated EOM, Net30 payment terms.
- 6% channel holdback recorded as "Escrow: Channel holdback" on Redwood invoice and retained for 90 days.
- ByteChannel claim evidence: signed usage report + DataMill billing CSV export OR our two-line signed template (either is OK).
- Release cadence: per-invoice at 90 days after invoice date; Redwood Ops validates within 3 business days of claim.
- Accounting: holdback treated as contra-revenue until release; list price and private-offer discount unchanged.

Next steps / immediate actions:
1) Ops runbook call Thursday 21 May 14:00 PT — invite sent (30m). Attendees: Hannah, Ben, Irene, Maya, Evelyn.
2) I'll create a short DocuSign addendum covering the holdback terms (RDW-ESCROW-ADD-1) and share with your procurement lead.
3) Post-call: finalize escrow-runbook-v1.md and publish the runbook link for ByteChannel to submit claims.

Attachments: link to runbook draft + redwood-privoffer-summary.pdf (already attached in the thread).

If anything else pops up before the call, ping me. Looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Cloud GTM — Redwood Inference
